earlyBlight.description: Early blight is a widespread fungal disease that attacks tomato and potato foliage, stems, and fruit, producing distinct target-shaped rings.
symptoms: Concentric ring lesions (target spots) on mature lower leaves
Yellow chlorotic halos surrounding brown necroses
Stem cankers near ground level in severe cases
Premature leaf yellowing and defoliation progressing upward

organic: Apply Cold-Pressed Neem Oil spray (5ml per liter of soft water) every 7 days
Spray Copper Soap (Copper Octanoate) at first sign of spots
Bio-fungicide drench with Bacillus subtilis or Trichoderma viride
chemical: Azoxystrobin 23% SC (1ml / liter) for targeted translaminar control
Chlorothalonil 75% WP (2g / liter) on alternate weeks

prevention: Maintain adequate 60cm row spacing to maximize airflow
Mulch heavily with clean straw to prevent soil splashback onto foliage
Strictly avoid overhead irrigation; use drip watering at soil base
Rotate solanaceous crops on a 3-year cycle

powderyMildew.description: A powdery white fungal coating covering leaves and shoots, reducing photosynthesis and fruit size.
symptoms: White talcum powder-like fungal patches on leaf surfaces
Leaves crinkle, cup upwards, and show stunted growth
Premature leaf drop exposing fruit to sunburn

organic: Spray diluted milk whey (1 part milk to 9 parts water) in morning sun
Potassium bicarbonate spray (3g / liter of water)
Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) foliar wash

prevention: Prune dense canopy to ensure sun penetration through foliage
Avoid high nitrogen over-fertilization which promotes succulent leaves

healthy.description: The leaf tissue displays uniform chlorophyll saturation, vibrant cell structure, and no visible fungal or viral damage.
symptoms: Uniform rich green pigmentation
Sturdy vascular vein network without chlorosis
Intact leaf margins and unblemished cuticle

organic: Continue balanced seaweed extract bio-stimulant foliar nutrition

prevention: Monitor weekly using sticky traps for preventive pest scouting
